Intra-group conflict occurs within a single group when members hold differing opinions or ideas regarding how to achieve their common goals. Essentially, while the group is united by a shared objective, the internal disagreement over the "how" or the "what" creates friction among the members. This type of conflict can lead to divisions within the group and ultimately hinder progress toward achieving those collective objectives (note 1.pdf).

To understand this, you can think of it like a sports team where every player wants to win the championship (the common goal), but some teammates argue that the team should focus on a defensive strategy while others insist on an aggressive offensive strategy. Because they cannot agree on the method to reach their goal, the team becomes divided, which may prevent them from playing effectively and winning the game.

[AI-GENERATED EXAMPLE]
Imagine a student project group tasked with creating a presentation. All members want to get an 'A' grade. However, two members want to use a slide-heavy format to explain the data, while the other two members want to use a video-based format. Because they cannot agree on the best way to present their research, they spend their meeting time arguing about the format instead of actually completing the work, which slows down their progress and creates tension within the group.

The provided materials do not offer a step-by-step process for resolving intra-group conflict, though they do note generally that conflicts are best resolved when "nibbed in the bud" at an early stage before they escalate (note 1.pdf).
